claim_being_audited: The Actor claims the model can be certified for launch because aggregate readiness passed and rollout controls exist, provided the known enterprise refund workflow limitation is explicitly disclosed in the model card before launch rather than treated as cured by rollout controls alone.
specific_concerns: The admissible record supports the existence of a material exposed limitation in a named launch use case.
The policy text says rollout controls do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The risk acceptance draft is unapproved and does not address the exposed enterprise refund workflow segment.
There is no admissible evidence that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed before launch.

The Actor's packet is directionally consistent with the evidence, but the recommended action 'certify_model' is stronger than the current record supports unless certification is explicitly conditioned on completed disclosure.
unsupported_claims: Any unqualified claim that the model is presently certifiable on the existing record alone.
Any implication that a 4% rollout, rollback switch, or monitoring dashboard can substitute for required disclosure.
Any implication that risk acceptance covers this limitation.
evidence_requests: Provide the final pre-launch model card or approval artifact showing explicit disclosure of the enterprise refund workflow limitation.
Provide any approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses enterprise refund workflow exposure, if such approval exists.
Clarify whether certification is being granted conditionally on disclosure completion or has already been granted unconditionally.
decision_criteria: Aggregate readiness and lack of severity-one rehearsal incidents support launch readiness but do not by themselves satisfy model-card disclosure policy.
A material limitation in a named launch use case must be resolved, disclosed, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Because the affected enterprise refund workflow segment remains exposed in the rollout cohort, rollout controls cannot substitute for disclosure.
A conditional certification rationale can be derived from the evidence, but an unconditional certification decision cannot.
